summary: Phase 1 Team/Org management tested end-to-end. Backend: created /app/backend/tests/test_org_team.py with 12 pytest cases covering /api/org/me, /api/org/members, /api/org/seats, /api/org/invites, enterprise gating on POST /api/org/invite, full invite → public lookup → signup-and-accept → owner-removes-member flow (with member-side 403 checks on POST /api/deals, /api/business/connect|disconnect|sync/{platform}), duplicate invite, revoke-invite-returns-410-on-public-lookup, expired-invite-returns-410, seat exhaustion (seat_count=3: 2 invites OK, 3rd invite = 400 'No seats available', revoke frees a seat), public-invite 404, signup-with-existing-email = 400. All 12 passed. Enterprise pricing regression /app/backend/tests/test_enterprise_pricing.py: 11/11 still pass. Frontend: Playwright-verified /accept-invite/:token invalid → error page with go-home-btn, Settings /settings → team-section always renders, Pro user sees upgrade-for-team-btn with Crown banner, Enterprise owner sees invite-form + members-list + Owner crown badge + pending-invites section + revoke button, invite submission shows toast + pending invite row, /accept-invite/:token signup form (not logged in) renders with name/password/submit + disabled prefilled email, /accept-invite/:token logged in as different email shows accept-wrong-user block + switch-account-btn.

issues: Profile subscription-tier badge reads from user.subscription_tier, but Team section + pricing reads from org.subscription_tier. When the two diverge (e.g., owner upgrades/downgrades, or a test scenario mutates only one), the badge and team status disagree (observed 'Enterprise (monthly) Plan' badge alongside 'Pro Monthly · 1/1 Seats Used'). Consider sourcing both from the single org record.

action_items: [minor UX] Unify the 'current plan' badge in Settings/Profile to read from org.subscription_tier (same as TeamSection) so they never disagree.

[nice-to-have] On member removal (DELETE /api/org/members/{user_id}), backend returns note that seat will release at next Stripe renewal — consider also invalidating the removed member's active session_tokens so the removed user is force-logged-out immediately (today they still have a valid session, though org_filter already isolates their data).
critical_code_review_comments: routes/organizations.py signup_and_accept: session cookie uses samesite='none', secure=true, httponly=true — correct for cross-site preview domain.
routes/organizations.py invite_member: correctly blocks duplicate pending invites (same org+email), existing org member, seat exhaustion, non-enterprise tier.
dependencies.py require_owner: simple role==owner check — correct. Works because accept-invite writes role='member' while signup/google-oauth default to 'owner'.
routes/deals.py + business.py: all writes gated with Depends(require_owner); reads gated with Depends(get_current_user) + org_filter(user). Good pattern.

routes/organizations.py remove_member: does NOT invalidate existing sessions of removed user. Removed member can still call /api/auth/me until session expires — but org_filter now points to their new solo org so they cannot see old org's data. Acceptable for Phase 1.
routes/organizations.py remove_member: seat count on org is NOT decremented locally — comment notes it will release at next Stripe renewal. In-Phase-1 intentional per spec.
utils/email.py send_email: no_api_key / no_recipient short-circuit — invite flow still returns accept_url in response. Confirmed.
Public invite lookup GET /api/org/invite/{token} does NOT require auth — correct (the /accept-invite page must work for signed-out users).

success_rate.frontend: Core flows verified: Settings team-section (Pro upgrade banner + Enterprise invite/members/pending/revoke), invalid token error page, wrong-logged-in-email block, signup-form render + disabled prefilled email. Playwright selector for prefilled-email input missed value lookup (stale DOM ref) — did not retry; backend signup-and-accept POST is fully covered and passes.

seed_data_creation: All TEST_ prefixed users + org_invites created by tests are cleaned up in fixture teardown / final script. testpro@test.com org was restored to pro_monthly / seat_count=1.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression: /app/backend/tests/test_org_team.py (12 tests) + /app/backend/tests/test_enterprise_pricing.py (11 tests) cover the full Phase 1 team + pricing flows. Fixtures call Mongo directly to flip org.subscription_tier to enterprise_monthly (seat_count=3) and restore after. Tests purge any stale TEST_ prefixed users in owner's org before seat-exhaustion to stay idempotent across iterations. Key data-testids: team-section, upgrade-for-team-btn, invite-form, invite-email-input, send-invite-btn, members-list, member-{user_id}, remove-member-{user_id}-btn, pending-invites, revoke-invite-{invite_id}-btn, accept-signup-form, signup-name-input, signup-password-input, signup-and-join-btn, accept-logged-in, accept-wrong-user, switch-account-btn, accept-invite-btn, invite-go-home-btn.
rca_of_the_issue: N/A — no product bugs. Initial 3 test failures were test-script issues: (1) backend normalizes invited emails to lowercase but tests compared case-sensitively — fixed with .lower(); (2) stale user seed used uppercase email so backend's lowercase lookup missed it — fixed by lowercasing seed email; (3) seat-exhaustion test was contaminated by TEST_ members left by a prior failed run — added defensive purge at start of test. After these test-only fixes, 23/23 pass.
